# Account Relationship Management

`customer_support.support_management.account_relationship_management` · v0.1.0 · **draft** · **STUB**

**Where does the support relationship with this account actually stand, between tickets?**


> Holding a support relationship with a named account across time, rather than answering its tickets one at a time. This is the technical-account-management motion: the same people, a known environment, a history of what has already gone wrong, and a standing obligation that does not reset when a ticket closes. The unit of work is the relationship, so the signals that matter are the ones no single ticket contains — an account that has stopped writing in, a new named contact nobody has met, an escalation that was resolved technically and never repaired socially. It is also where support silence is read correctly: from an account that used to file tickets, quiet is a warning rather than a result.

> Promote by adding outcomes, failure_modes, playbooks, heuristics, mental_models, decision_frameworks, kpis and handoffs, following quality-assurance in this subdomain. This is the capability that owns the two situations in this domain binding `champion_quiet` and `intro_followup`, which makes it one of the few able to route on day one — see situations/named-contact-gone-quiet.yaml and situations/new-account-contact.yaml. The expertise worth encoding first is the inversion against sales: sales reads a quiet contact as neutral and support should read it as decay, because a supported account that has stopped asking for help has usually either solved its problem elsewhere or stopped expecting us to solve it. Second is that contact-handover moments are where entitlement knowledge is lost, and the first experience a new named contact has sets the tone for the remainder of the contract.
